To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the linguistic insights of LFG can be reformulated within a resource-sensitive logic, that the Curry-Howard correspondence can be used to interpret the logic semantically, and that the resulting logic is expressive enough to capture the linguistic phenomena that motivated the introduction of non-monotonic mechanisms in LFG.
the linguistic insights and intutitions of LFG are compatible with the use of a substructural modal propositional logic, and that this logic is also compatible with a Curry–Howard interpretation.

(a) the fundamental linguistic insights of LFG can be captured in a resource sensitive logic with a Curry–Howard style semantics; (b) this resource sensitive logic can express some linguistic phenomena that require non-monotonic reasoning in LFG; and (c) the Curry–Howard correspondence can provide an alternative to the usual denotational semantic approach to LFG.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether a “resource sensitive interpretation” of LFG can be developed, which is based on a multi-modal logic.
a new approach to linguistic theory based on resource sensitive logic.
the possibility that the fundamental insights of LFG can be expressed within a framework that is both more expressive and more mathematically tractable than the usual LFG framework.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the approach presented here is a viable alternative to LFG.
this approach to LFG is a very promising direction for future work.
this work provides a novel and interesting perspective on LFG and its relation to other linguistic theories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a new way to look at the LFG theory.
we have provided a new perspective for LFG, in which the f-structure can be seen as an expression of resource sensitivity.
the LFG's f-description based analysis of natural languages can be reformulated as a substructural modal analysis of natural languages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fundamental linguistic insights of LFG are independent of the specific computational mechanisms used to express them.

a resource sensitive approach to syntax provides an alternative way of expressing the same linguistic insights as LFG, but without the use of the nonmonotonic “constraint equations” and “constraint-based” machinery of LFG.
LFG's insights and intuitional basis can be captured in a resource sensitive framework that has been used to model other linguistic phenomena.
